findings.text: Releasing a block cache entry drops its reference count and, while references remain, wakes waiters only when the remaining count is small; when the last reference is gone the entry is handed to the cache free path.

Board description for the PC compatible clock carries optional wake control callbacks, a flags word, an address space selector, and register indices for day alarm, month alarm and century, where zero means the feature is absent.

Time and date indices assign seconds to 0 and seconds alarm to 1, minutes to 2 and minutes alarm to 3, hours to 4 and hours alarm to 5, weekday to 6, month day to 7, month to 8 and year to 9, with control and status registers at 10, 11, 12 and 13; frequency select aliases the first control register, control the second, interrupt flags the third, and validity the fourth.
First control register encodings use an update busy flag and divider mask, three reference clock selections, two divider reset codes, an AMD bank bit, and a low nibble rate mask.

Second control register provides set, periodic enable, alarm enable, update enable, square wave, binary mode, twenty four hour mode and daylight saving bits; the third reports any interrupt with periodic, alarm and update pendings; the fourth carries a validity flag; a wildcard value marks alarm fields as do not care.

I/O sizing defines a total extent with a smaller used extent in one configuration and used equal to total in the other, a default I/O mapped indicator, and a board flag bit requesting no frequency handling.

Address encryption helpers exist in two configurations: one toggles an encryption mask to produce encrypted, canonical and cleared forms, and one where all conversions are identity operations leaving the input unchanged.
Hardware poison tracking node couples an interval tree entry with an address space pointer and a callback translating a page frame number to a virtual memory area offset.
Registration of that tracking node in this configuration always reports operation not supported, while unregistration accepts the pointer and performs no action.

Memory grouping descriptor holds a node identifier, a list of member blocks, counts of present kernel and movable pages, a dynamic flag, and a variant payload giving either maximum pages for static groups or unit pages for dynamic groups.
Block hotplug lifecycle moves among online, going offline, offline, going online, and cancel states for interrupted transitions, with the first three exposed to user space as text.

Hotplug block descriptor records starting section number, lifecycle state, requested online type, node identity, an optional single zone when all managed ranges share it, embedded device object, alternate map pointer, owning group pointer and group linkage, plus an optional poison counter when failure and hotplug combine.
The lifecycle state field of the hotplug block is serialized by the embedded device lock.
Range to block alignment rounds the start up and the end down to block boundaries and yields an empty range when no whole block fits, otherwise returning an inclusive aligned span.
Hotplug notification payload carries a starting page frame number and a page count describing the affected span.
Hotplug notifier ordering assigns default zero, slab one, CXL five, HMAT six, compute batching and cpuset ten, and tiering and KSM one hundred.

Without hotplug support, device initialization, notifier registration and unregistration, notification dispatch and hotplug registration succeed trivially without effect, advised size query returns zero, and size advice reports missing device.
Dropping a block reference releases the embedded device object; traversal helpers define callbacks visiting a block or a group with opaque caller data and reporting status.
Hotplug subscription helper creates a boot resident notifier block binding a handler and priority and registers it immediately.
Block identity helpers derive a block number from a section number by division, from a page frame via its section, and from a physical address via its page frame.
Minimum block size is one shifted by the section size bit count.
Memory region descriptor pairs a target node identifier with an address range.
Region identifier allocation in this configuration always fails with out of memory while freeing accepts an identifier and does nothing.

Cache maintenance query reports absence of invalidation support, range invalidation warns once and fails with missing device, and full invalidation delegates to range invalidation covering the entire address space.
Requesting CPU cache invalidation when the platform lacks support triggers a one time warning and returns failure, so callers must treat lack of support as an error rather than silent success.
Per resource accounting holds a configured maximum and atomic counters for high watermark, current usage, and event counts both hierarchical and local.
Misc controller state embeds the subsystem state, two event files for hierarchical and local views, and an array of per resource trackers sized by the resource type count.
Resource type enumeration optionally includes AMD SEV, SEV-ES and Intel TDX identifiers depending on build options, always terminated by a count sentinel.

Conversion from subsystem state to controller state is null safe via container lookup; current task lookup and reference release handle null gracefully in one configuration and always yield null or no action in the stub; capacity and charging operations in the stub succeed trivially.
Legacy mouse and pad minors assign PS2 mouse to 1, with unused bus mouse ids at 2 and 3, unused Atari, Sun and Apollo at 5, 6 and 7, and unused PC110 pad at 9.

System service minors place watchdog at 130, temperature at 131, APM at 134, RTC at 135, VHCI at 137, openprom at 139, unused DMAPI at 140, NVRAM at 144, SBUS flash at 152, SGI timer at 153, PMU at 154, unused store queue at 155, LCD at 156, AC at 157 and button at 158.
Further control minors assign flash at 160, environment at 162, I2O at 166, user control at 174, AGP at 175, Toshiba at 181 and hardware random at 183.

Input and virtualization minors assign keypad to 185, IR net to 187, seven segment to 193, VFIO to 196, PXA graphics to 197, TUN to 200, CUSE to 203, MPT family to 220, 221 and 222, uinput to 223, mcelog to 227 and HPET to 228.

Remaining minors place FUSE at 229, snapshot at 231, KVM at 232, btrfs at 234, autofs at 235, device mapper control at 236, loop control at 237, vhost net at 238, HID and user I/O at 239 and 240, vsock and EISA EEPROM sharing 241, RFKILL at 242, with dynamic allocation sentinel at 255.
Misc device descriptor carries a minor number, name, file operations pointer, list linkage, parent and self device pointers, sysfs groups, node name and mode.
Registration helpers bind a misc device to built-in or modular driver lifecycle with automatic register and deregister, plus an alias generator encoding the misc major and minor.
Filesystem identity wrappers encapsulate a user identifier and a group identifier respectively in single field structures.
A mount identity map is considered valid only when it is neither the no-op map nor the invalid marker.
Value extraction has two configurations: one returning the stored identifier and one always yielding zero regardless of input, for both user and group wrappers.

Validity means the extracted value differs from all bits set; equality requires the left side valid and numeric equality of extracted values, with cross type comparisons against kernel identifiers following the same validity gate.

Construction helpers build filesystem identities from kernel identifiers and define invalid sentinels from invalid kernel ids, with inverse helpers rebuilding kernel identifiers from filesystem identities.

Mapping probes test whether an identity has a filesystem mapping via translation validity or has an identifier mapping via namespace translation, with direct conversions and current credential mappings built on the same translation helpers.
CPU modalias entry carries a single sixteen bit feature code.
Buffered writeback helper forwards mapping, control and block lookup to the common multi page write path with no auxiliary buffer argument.

Multi precision integer descriptor records allocated limb count, used limb count, informative bit count, sign, flag word with secure allocation and indirection meanings, and a pointer to the limb array, with limbs defined as machine word sized values and sizes derived from bits per word.
Byte size helper multiplies the used limb count by the per limb byte width.
Media validation accepts descriptors at or above F8 hex or exactly F0 hex, rejecting all other values.

Master boot record partition entry packs boot flag, start geometry triple, type code, end geometry triple, and little endian start sector and sector count, with table magic AA55 hex, stored without padding.
Partition type codes distinguish extended variants, Linux data, LVM and RAID autodetect, Solaris pair, Disk Manager helpers and EZ drive, BSD family, Minix and Unixware identifiers.
Socket option transfer descriptor couples input and output iterators with an option length.
